doc.title: Grover Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, February 13, 1996

title: Mostly white festival audiences
summary: Asked about white festival audiences, Mitchell cites poverty and media structure, noting many black people do not know Basie or Parker.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What do you make of the fact that festivals like this one, when the audience seems to be almost totally white?

Well again we’re back to this social structure and the social division and then you’ve got to figure that most black people are poor and they can’t afford it. That’s a fact. And the funny thing about it is, we’re talking about jazz came out of the black community, but the

people that don’t know anything about jazz are the first ones to say I never heard of Count Basie or Charlie Parker is a black person. You know? Somehow or other they’re — it’s the media structure and the huge warehousing in these areas and neighborhoods and all that kind of stuff, it creates dumb stuff.
